N.C.D.N. 16:7:1919. THE NORTH
BREST, LITOVSK NO. 2.
THE THREAT FROM RUSSIA'S DESPERATION.
KOLTCHAK'S FEEBLE HOLD.
A RUSSIAN'S ACCOUNT OF THINGS THE ALLIES HAVE
NEVER UNDERSTOOD.

Mr. D. A. Lunden, a Russian who is on his way to Washington and London to make representations with reference to the situation in Siberia, is at present in Shanghai. A native of Central Russia, he is 28 years of age, and like many of his countrymen is an expert linguist, talking, in addition to his native tongue, English, French, Italian and German. He studied mathematics in the University of Liege, and has also graduated at King's College, London. While there he organized an Anglo-Russian Society at the University. Following the revolution in 1917 he went to Petrograd where he stayed for a time, meeting most of the eminent politicians there, and thereafter went to Vladivostok, where he represented "The Times." At that time he organized an Anglo-Russian Society there, his object being to bring about a real alliance between England and Russia.

As stated, he is now on his way to the United States and England in connexion with the political state of Russia, and to a representative of the "North-China Daily News" he yesterday gave his views upon the condition of affairs in his country.

Fighting The Bolsheviks.

Last year, said Mr. Lunden, General Knox, as representative of the British Military Mission, came to Siberia, where there was a kind of government known as the Siberian Government. It is sufficient to say that this government was in close contact with the Zemstvos, which, as you know, are a union of towns and even villages acting on the basis of autonomy. While I admit that those who were in the Siberian Government were too weak to rule and too weak to fight the Bolsheviks, their intentions were honest and, I should say, correct. At that time many members of the Constituent Assembly had a conference in Ufa, and they formed the well-known Directorium at the head of which was the famous Avksientiev, the social revolutionary, who was certainly opposed to Bolshevism in any shape or form. Although many people say that this Directorium was too weak to fight the Bolsheviks, I am not of that opinion. Suppose at the beginning this organization was weak, it was extremely powerful to inspire the population to take up arms against the Bolsheviks for the following reason. First of all it was prepared and ready to act in close contact with the Zemstvos. These institu-
tions are extremely popular in Russia, and are trusted by the greatest majority of the populace I do not intend to give you any idea of the numbers which stand for the Zemstvos, but I think it will be sufficient to tell you that the great bulk of the peasants do stand for them, and, as we know, the peasants are the propelling force in Russia, although very nearly in a latent state. Although that organization from a military or diplomatic point of view was weak—perhaps I would admit that—it was a tremendous force which could collect all the real forces of Russia, including the peasants, inspire them, and show them the nearest hope to get a real constitutional assembly where the people would be represented and would shape the real future of Russia. Of course, it would come out a republic.

If this organization, the Directorium, had had the full support of the Allies, their real sympathy and their real help economically and in sending munitions, without sending a single foreign soldier to Russia, it would certainly have succeeded in inspiring the populace to form an army and march on Moscow, overthrowing the dictatorship of this one class, the Bolsheviks, and calling a Russian parliament together.

Enter the Bureaucrats.

But let us see what happened at this time. You must remember that after the Revolution a great number of the bureaucrats, including civilians and military men, did not like the word "freedom" at all. Not because it was a danger to the Russian people, but it really spelt failure and destruction to their dark ambitions of the old days of the Tsar's régime. What was the result? They had to leave Central Russia, where more or less the socialists were in power, and fly to Siberia, to the Crimea and some other places outside the centre of European Russia. Some perhaps, especially the officers, were terrorized by the Bolsheviks.

These people, being outside the heart of Russia, became inspired, I should say, with vengeance, the French revanche. Being blinded by that idea, they never considered the object of having Russia a free country, and they organized themselves to fight those whom they called their enemies, not declaring to the Russian people what would happen in case they succeeded. As every bureaucrat is, these people were terrible cowards, and they did not dare to take up arms in sup-

来自俄罗斯绝望状态的威胁。
高尔察克脆弱的控制。
一名俄国人讲述协约国从未理解的事实。

D. A. Lunden 先生，一名正前往华盛顿和伦敦就西伯利亚局势进行交涉的俄国人，目前身在上海。他是俄罗斯中部人，现年 28 岁，像许多同胞一样，他是一位精通语言的人，除母语外，还能说英语、法语、意大利语和德语。他曾在列日大学学习数学，并在伦敦国王学院毕业。在那里期间，他在大学组织了一个英俄协会。1917 年革命后，他前往彼得格勒，在那里停留了一段时间，会见了当地大多数著名政治家，随后前往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴），代表《泰晤士报》工作。当时他在那里组织了一个英俄协会，其目的是促成英国和俄罗斯之间的真正联盟。

如前所述，他目前正因俄罗斯的政治状况前往美国和英国，并于昨日向《字林西报》的一名代表阐述了他对祖国局势的看法。

对抗布尔什维克。

Lunden 先生说，去年，诺克斯将军作为英国军事代表团代表来到西伯利亚，那里有一个被称为西伯利亚政府的政府。 suffice it to say（ suffice it to say 意为“ suffice it to say”或“只需指出”）这个政府与地方自治局（Zemstvos）保持着密切联系，众所周知，地方自治局是基于自治原则运作的城镇甚至村庄的联盟。虽然我承认西伯利亚政府中的人员统治能力太弱，对抗布尔什维克的力量也太弱，但他们的意图是诚实的，我认为也是正确的。当时，制宪会议的许多成员在乌法举行会议，他们组成了著名的执政内阁（Directorium），由著名的社会革命党人阿夫克森季耶夫（Avksientiev）领导，他当然反对任何形式的布尔什维主义。虽然许多人说这个执政内阁对抗布尔什维克的力量太弱，但我并不这么认为。假设这个组织在初期很薄弱，但它具有极大的力量去激励民众拿起武器对抗布尔什维克，原因如下。首先，它准备就绪，并愿意与地方自治局密切合作。这些机构在俄罗斯极受欢迎，并受到绝大多数民众的信任。我不打算向您提供支持地方自治局的人数概念，但我认为告诉您广大农民都支持它们就足够了，而且我们知道，尽管几乎处于潜伏状态，农民却是俄罗斯的推动力。虽然从军事或外交角度来看，该组织是薄弱的——也许我会承认这一点——但它是一股巨大的力量，能够集结俄罗斯的所有真实力量，包括农民，激励他们，并向他们展示获得一个真正的、人民有代表权并能塑造俄罗斯真正未来的制宪会议的最接近的希望。当然，结果将是一个共和国。

如果这个组织，即执政内阁，得到了协约国的全力支持，得到他们真正的同情以及经济和军火输送方面的真正帮助，而不向俄罗斯派遣一兵一卒，它肯定能成功激励民众组建军队并向莫斯科进军，推翻布尔什维克这一阶级的独裁统治，并召集俄罗斯议会。

官僚登场。

但让我们看看当时发生了什么。您必须记住，革命后，大量官僚，包括文职和军方人员，根本不喜欢“自由”这个词。这并不是因为它对俄罗斯人民构成危险，而是因为它确实意味着他们在沙皇政权旧时代的黑暗野心的失败和毁灭。结果如何？他们不得不离开社会主义者或多或少掌权的俄罗斯中部，逃往西伯利亚、克里米亚以及欧洲俄罗斯中心以外的一些其他地方。有些人，特别是军官，可能受到了布尔什维克的恐吓。

这些人身处俄罗斯心脏地带之外，我想说，他们被复仇的念头所激发，就像法国的复仇主义一样。被这种想法蒙蔽了双眼，他们从未考虑过让俄罗斯成为一个自由国家的目标，而是组织起来对抗他们所谓的敌人，并未向俄罗斯人民宣告如果他们成功会发生什么。正如每个官僚那样，这些人都是可怕的懦夫，他们不敢拿起武器支

page_data.en:
port of their cause until the Allies
came to Russia. Then they had to
try to form some sort of military
organisation.
Here is another item of Russian
politics and concerning Russia
generally. When the Allies came
to Russia they did not come in con-
tact with the Zemstvos. They did
not try, or perhaps they did not
understand how to do it—to mix
with the people, find out the real
opinion of the people and on such
an opinion base their policy of in-
tervention. They came in contact
with the militarists, and instead of
supporting Avksentiev, or any
body in contact with the Zemstvos
simply decided to have a kind of
military dictatorship.

Koltchak's Dictatorship.

I do not attempt to say that the
Allies did it because they liked it
I presume they did not understand
the situation: that is more likely.
Since they decided to have a mili-
tary dictatorship, whom could they
choose to support? The only man
was Koltchak, and that for this
reason, that Koltchak, who was a
Vice-Admiral in the Black Sea, be-
came more or less popular during
the Revolution. Koltchak is a
very good patriot and honest, but
Koltchak is very weak. I think
his health is also very bad, and he
is a very nervous person. It stands
to reason that as soon as a naval
or military man became head of
the government, all the militarists
collected round him, and became
very powerful in the government's
policy.
I am not going to discuss how the
army was formed, but at the be-
ginning, especially, Koltchak's
army was successful. They were
approaching Kazan and Samara—
already in the centre of European
Russia. At that moment the situa-
tion was worse than ever for the
following reason. The militarists
became cocksure that they would
take Moscow; they started to sup-
pose that their policy was the right
one, and they had some proof, for
they had their army near Kazan,
near Samara. At that moment
what they had really need of was
to have all the sympathy of the
Russian people. But they forgot
about the Constituent Assembly,
they arrested many people of the
Zemstvos, and many really honest
and true sons of Russia have been
compelled to leave the country be-
cause they stood more or less for
the real principle of the Russian
people. Well, as soon as the Rus-
sians began to realize that this
organization or so-called govern-
ment of Koltchak's more or less
resembled the old conditions of
serfdom, they turned their backs
upon it. At that very moment the
Allies had a very real need of in-
formation, but they were always
misinformed. As far back as April
26 I pointed out here in Shanghai,
when Koltchak was already near
Samara and Kazan, that the situa-
tion was still worse, but no one
paid the slightest attention to my
words. The government had for-
gotten to conquer the sympathies
of the people, they forgot to speak
of the rights of the people.

Why Koltchak Must Fail.

Even supposing that Koltchak
stands for the principles of free-
dom, at that time he had become
too weak to oppose his companions.
If he had opposed them, it meant
to say it would be almost a victory
for the Bolsheviks. I am a
mathematician, and I consider
things from a logical and psycholo-
gical point of view. You can
never plant a tree with the roots
in the air; they must be in the
soil. And the government of
Koltchak was exactly the same
thing, the roots were in the air
instead of in the soil. Unless a
man gives a programme of what
he wishes to do for the Russian
people, he will fail even if he suc-
ceeds temporarily in taking Mos-
cow. Those who go with the peo-
ple, who go with the Zemstvos, will
certainly succeed in overthrowing
any tyranny, be it from the right
or left. For the present I think
that gives the real reason why
Koltchak is unsuccessful—and of
course he is going to be more un-
successful in the very near future,
because by giving up Ufa and
Perm, which are the real indus-
trial centres in the Urals, where
they make munitions and artillery,
it seems to me that his forces must
be disorganized. I personally do
not believe for a second that he will
succeed in keeping Omsk, and the
very near future will show it.

Lotteries and Race Courses.

I admit that for non-Russian
people to understand Russia you
require much more information
than I give you just now. But I
do say this: whenever I open an
English paper here, I do not think
it would be a very rude word to
say, I am disgusted. I find two
or three columns of lotteries and
baseball and race courses, but not
a single attempt is made by the
Press to study the situation in
Russia. Do you realize how im-
portant it is? Do you know that
if Russia is in desperation for an-
other few months the peace with
Germany will become Brest-Litovsk
No. 2. My advice is that the Press
should pay the closest attention to
Russian politics, and not jump to
conclusions. For instance one or
two papers here in Shanghai used
to write in not many lines on the
following subject:—Koltchak is
going to save Russia, Koltchak is
going to become the head of the
government, and will perhaps suc-
ceed in taking Moscow and so on.
These people based their theories
on some very ordinary informa-
tion, but you know we cannot
study a thing from a psychological
point of view on an ordinary
telegram. The foreign correspon-
dents in Russia, I think, write
very bad despatches to the English
and American Press. Eighty per
cent. of them are occupied telling
stories about Russia, and they do
not give the situation. That is
why the situation is misunderstood.

Bolshevism In Siberia.

All the foreign correspondents
wrote that Bolshevism is finished
in Siberia: I wrote that it is not.
The reason is that I came in con-
tact with the people, and they did
not, and in consequence they had
to collect their information from
second-hand sources. The result is
waste of time, waste of energy, and
waste of life, not only Russian but
Allied.
Do not make the fatal mistake
that this giant is going to die, that
it can be cut to pieces. Except the
Poles and Finns and perhaps the
Esthonians, all nationalities stand
for a united Russia. Even the
Ukrainians will ultimately join
with Russia, for they are Russians,
they are Slavs.

（批：3233 / 19/8/20）
page_data.zh:
支持其事业，直到协约国来到俄国。随后，他们不得不试图组建某种军事组织。

这是关于俄国政治及一般俄国事务的另一事项。当协约国来到俄国时，他们并未与地方自治局（Zemstvos）接触。他们并未尝试，或者也许是不懂得如何去做——去融入民众，查明民众的真实意见，并以此类意见为基础制定其干涉政策。他们接触的是军人集团，并且没有支持阿夫克森季耶夫（Avksentiev）或任何与地方自治局有联系的人，而是简单地决定实行某种形式的军事独裁。

高尔察克的独裁统治。

我并非试图说协约国这样做是因为他们喜欢这样。我推测他们是不了解局势：这更有可能。既然他们决定实行军事独裁，他们能选择支持谁呢？唯一的人选是高尔察克（Koltchak），其原因在于，高尔察克曾是黑海舰队的海军少将，在革命期间变得颇受欢迎。高尔察克是一位非常爱国且诚实的人，但高尔察克非常软弱。我认为他的健康状况也很糟糕，而且他是一个神经过敏的人。理所当然地，一旦一名海军或军人成为政府首脑，所有军人集团便聚集在他周围，并在政府政策中变得极具影响力。

我不打算讨论军队是如何组建的，但在初期，尤其是高尔察克的军队曾取得成功。他们逼近喀山（Kazan）和萨马拉（Samara）——已处于欧洲俄国的中心地带。在那一刻，局势比以往任何时候都更糟，原因如下。军人集团确信他们将攻占莫斯科；他们开始认为他们的政策是正确的，并且他们有一些证据，因为他们的军队已在喀山附近、萨马拉附近。在那一刻，他们真正需要的是获得全体俄国人民的同情。但他们忘记了立宪会议，逮捕了许多地方自治局的人员，许多真正诚实和忠贞的俄罗斯之子被迫离开本国，因为他们或多或少地代表了俄国人民的真正原则。好吧，一旦俄国人开始意识到这个组织或所谓的高尔察克政府或多或少类似于旧的农奴制条件，他们便背弃了它。就在那一刻，协约国非常需要情报，但他们总是得到错误的情报。早在4月26日，我就在上海指出，当高尔察克已逼近萨马拉和喀山时，局势仍然更加恶化，但没有人对我的话给予丝毫关注。政府忘记了去赢得人民的同情，忘记了去谈论人民的权利。

高尔察克为何必然失败。

即使假设高尔察克代表自由的原则，在当时他也已变得过于软弱，无法反对他的同伴。如果他反对他们，那就意味着这几乎将成为布尔什维克的胜利。我是一名数学家，我从逻辑和心理学的角度看待事物。你永远不能种植根部朝上的树；根部必须在土壤中。而高尔察克的政府正是如此，根部在空中而不是在土壤里。除非一个人给出他希望为俄国人民做什么的计划，否则即使他暂时成功攻占莫斯科，他也终将失败。那些与人民同行、与地方自治局同行的人，必将成功推翻任何暴政，无论其来自右翼还是左翼。目前我认为，这给出了高尔察克不成功的主要原因——当然，他在不久的将来会更加不成功，因为放弃乌法（Ufa）和彼尔姆（Perm），这两个是乌拉尔地区真正的工业中心，那里制造军火和大炮，在我看来，他的部队必定已经混乱不堪。我个人丝毫不相信他能成功守住鄂木斯克（Omsk），不久的将来将会证明这一点。

彩票与赛马场。

我承认，对于非俄国人来说，要理解俄国，你们需要比我刚才提供的更多的信息。但我确实要说：每当我在这里打开一份英文报纸时，我想说“令人厌恶”并不算粗鲁之词。我发现有两三栏关于彩票、棒球和赛马的内容，但媒体没有做出任何尝试去研究俄国的局势。你们意识到这有多重要吗？你们知道吗，如果俄国再绝望几个月，与德国的和平条约将成为第二个《布列斯特-立托夫斯克条约》。我的建议是，媒体应密切关注俄国政治，不要妄下结论。例如，上海的一两份报纸过去曾用寥寥数语报道以下主题：——高尔察克将拯救俄国，高尔察克将成为政府首脑，并可能成功攻占莫斯科等等。这些人基于一些非常普通的信息建立他们的理论，但你们知道，我们不能基于普通的电报从心理学角度研究事物。我认为，驻俄国的外国记者向英美媒体发出的通讯稿质量很差。百分之八十的记者忙于讲述关于俄国的故事，而没有反映真实局势。这就是局势被误解的原因。

西伯利亚的布尔什维主义。

所有外国记者都写道，布尔什维主义在西伯利亚已经结束：我写道事实并非如此。原因是我与民众进行了接触，而他们并没有，因此他们不得不从二手来源收集信息。结果是浪费时间、浪费精力，以及浪费生命，不仅是俄国的，也包括协约国的。

不要犯下致命的错误，认为这个巨人即将死去，认为它可以被肢解。除了波兰人、芬兰人，也许还有爱沙尼亚人，所有民族都主张一个统一的俄国。甚至乌克兰人最终也会加入俄国，因为他们是俄罗斯人，他们是斯拉夫人。

（批注：3233 / 19/8/20）

17th February, 1920. 191
REPORT ON Nationality of D. A. Lunder.
Made by D. S. I. Givens Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.
Sir,
There appears to be good reason to believe that
D. A. Lunden is a Russian subject. Mr. Tarasoff of the
Union of Siberian Co-Operative Companies with whom Lunden
lives at No. 133 Dixwell Road, states that the latter is
Russian, and other people with whom he has been in contact
corroborate this statement.
Lunden, who is a B. Sc. of London University, was
once the "Times" correspondent at Vladivostock. He is on
intimate terms with Miss Leda Yakovlevna, a typist, who
lives at No. 16A East Seward Road, and his description
is as follows : below medium height, about 35 years old,
wears pinc-nez glasses, clean shaven, front portion of
head bald, smart and well educated.
Efforts are now being made to confirm the
information that Lunden is Russian.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. S. I.
C. D. O.

先生，
似乎有充分理由相信 D. A. Lunden 是俄国臣民。西伯利亚合作公司联盟的 Tarasoff 先生（Lunden 与其同住于狄思威路133号）称，后者是俄国人，其他与他有过接触的人也证实了这一说法。

目前正在努力核实 Lunden 是俄国人的信息。
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
侦探副督察
首席侦探官

5th, February, 1920 191
REPORT ON Political Activities of Russians in Shanghai
Made by D. S. I. Givens Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.
Sir,
A group of local Russians, who call themselves
Social Democrats, are planning the formation of a society
of all democratic Russians in Shanghai who will elect a
committee to look after their interests. It is proposed
that this committee will take over the functions of the
Consul General for Russia until such time as the new
government in Siberia can nominate a man for this post.
The people advocating the dismissal of the
present Consul General for Russia allege that a representative
of the Koltchak Government, who was recently in Shanghai,
had Tls. 500,000.00 of Government funds in the Russo-Asiatic
Bank, and they say that the Russian Minister and Consular
officials in China are conferring with a view to finding
means to enrich themselves from public funds.
The scheme to hold a public meeting to protest
against Japanese intervention in Siberia originated with
the group of Russians above mentioned. Although they
would now seem to have given up hope of being able to
hold the meeting in the Settlement, they have not yet
abandoned the idea, and it is reported that the provisional
committee of which A. F. Agareff is President, and L. Hasser
is treasurer, will hold a meeting in the Russian Employment
Bureau, American ( Naval ) Y. M. C. A., Avenue Edward VII
[this evening] when plans to hold the meeting in Chinese
territory will be discussed. One of the Russians on the
provisional committee states that a number of influential

先生，
一群自称社会民主党的当地俄国人，正计划在上海成立一个全俄民主人士协会，该协会将选举一个委员会来维护他们的利益。提议该委员会将在西伯利亚新政府能够提名此人担任此职之前，接管俄国总领事的功能。
主张罢免现任俄国总领事的人声称，高尔察克政府的一名代表最近在上海，其在华俄道胜银行存有50万两政府资金，并称在华的俄国公使和领事官员正在商议，寻求从公款中牟利的方法。
举行公众集会抗议日本干涉西伯利亚的计划，源于上述俄国人群体。虽然他们现在似乎已放弃在租界内举行集会的希望，但他们尚未放弃这一想法，据报由 A. F. Agareff 任主席、L. Hasser 任司库的临时委员会，将于[今晚]在爱文义路美国（海军）青年会（Y. M. C. A.）的俄国人就业介绍所举行会议，届时将讨论在中国领土上举行集会的计划。临时委员会中的一名俄国人表示，许多有影响力的
